doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: After the war: nightclubs, Skitch Henderson, NBC and Ernie Kovacs
summary: He worked clubs, met Skitch Henderson, landed an NBC staff job via Faye Emerson, played with Ernie Kovacs and on Steve Allen's show.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: my way up, you know, after the war, worked in night clubs, The Copa and Bill Millers of the era, owned by that mythical organization. And met some people who were very helpful and still are. Skitch Henderson for example, who was a conductor, at that time a piano player with Frank Sinatra. And I found myself a job at NBC because Skitch’s lady friend, Faye Emerson, who was a wonderful movie star and a funny, bright woman, a beautiful woman, and she was a friend of Mr. Sarnoff which was very helpful. So I found myself on the staff of the radio at the — we called it the National Biscuit Company — but the NBC Broadcasting Company, and every once in a while I’d think, how did I get here? And I played in those days, I made friends with a comedian who I’d always liked, and I still think was one of the greatest comedians of all time, Ernie Kovacs, and Ernie and I became good friends and he always called me “Rosie.” I mean I didn’t have a first name or a last name, it was Rosie. And he was very good to me and he was going with Edie, his wife, it wasn’t his wife then, and I stayed at NBC and he had this wonderful crazy, zany show and I always wondered how it stayed on the air because he would do outrageous things. Sometimes he’d come in totally unprepared and just make it up as he went along. And it was like a quartet or a trio or something like that. And of course I learned, those were my vaudeville days. I learned how/what — somebody fell down — ketch ita boom. That kind of thing.

All the very classic things. And then, in those days the guy came along, Steve Allen, and we’re still good friends. Steve came along and they had the Sunday Night Show with a big orchestra, and Skitch was the conductor. I mean it just kind of moved around like that. And then recording sessions. And in that NBC Band were Doc Severinsen of course, he was the other young turk, but there were Will Bradley, a very well known trombone player and band leader at one time; Hymie Shertzer from the old Benny Goodman band; a whole bunch of people in that NBC staff and it was the job of jobs.
